source.title: I Bet Abliteration's Cost Was Sloppy Implementation. I Was Wrong

record.file_problem: None; the full post is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies an Arditi-style difference-in-means refusal-direction selection and ablation to a new model, Qwen3.5-27B, then evaluates refusal and TruthfulQA. The implementation is adapted for the model's hybrid attention.
record.gate_note: The layer 29, position -5, KL 0.034 result is reported as the direction-selection outcome, but is not a separate behavioral result row. Prior Arditi results are cited for comparison and are not rows. The post does not report an addition intervention.
record.test_reason: The study applies Arditi's difference-in-means direction selection and weight orthogonalization to a new model, Qwen3.5-27B, which needed an adapter for its hybrid attention. It measures refusal rate with substring matching on 39 prompts and capability on TruthfulQA MC1/MC2. It also compares HuiHui's released fixed-layer abliterated checkpoint. These are its own results on whether ablation removes refusal while keeping abilities (V1) and whether weight-edit abliteration works on a released model (V2).
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author bet that most of the TruthfulQA cost came from HuiHui's crude implementation, and found the opposite. Clean selection recovered only 0.73 (MC1) and 0.86 (MC2) points, so about 88% of the MC2 cost is intrinsic. Clean selection instead buys more complete refusal removal (0% vs 18%). The author attributes the cost to entanglement between refusal and TruthfulQA's refusal-adjacent content. The large size of the cost is left unexplained: smaller model, heavier safety tuning, or hybrid attention are offered as possibilities.
record.recipe_differences: Uses Arditi-style candidate selection and screening, adapted for Qwen3.5-27B's hybrid attention. The selected direction was at layer 29, position -5, and was orthogonalized out of weights writing to the residual stream. The author says this was not Arditi's identical pipeline.
record.method_sensitivity: The clean selected direction and HuiHui's fixed-layer, last-token direction produced different refusal rates (0% versus 18%) but similar TruthfulQA scores. The post also notes that its HF transformers backend differs from the earlier post's vLLM backend, so MC2 figures are not exactly comparable to that earlier post.
record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer review not stated
record.problems: The refusal evaluation uses 39 prompts, which the author calls a small sample. Refusal is initially flagged by substring matching; the author manually checked a sample of clean-model completions but does not report a formal uncertainty estimate. TruthfulQA is the only reported capability measure.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal. The selection pipeline screens candidates for it, but no induction result is reported. Capabilities other than TruthfulQA are not measured.
Released abliterated models other than HuiHui's Qwen3.5-27B. Whether the author's clean checkpoint was released is not stated.

record.verdict_notes: Single-author LessWrong post. The refusal set is small (39 prompts), refusal is flagged by substring matching with only a sampled manual check, and no uncertainty is reported. The KL value of 0.034 is a selection value, correctly kept out of the rows. Arditi's cited TruthfulQA results are comparison context, not rows. Base rows r1, r4 and r7 are references and correctly marked cannot_determine.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding the direction to induce refusals. TruthfulQA is the reported capability measure; other abilities are not evaluated.
Tests refusal after weight-edit ablation in HuiHui's model and the author's clean model, but not across released models generally. Whether the author's clean checkpoint was released is not stated.
Does not test attacks that suppress the direction or training against its ablation.
Does not test affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
Does not separately measure harmfulness judgments and refusal decisions.
Does not test cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer.
Does not vary refusal training. Possible effects of model size, safety tuning, and hybrid attention are raised as questions, not tested.

statements.correction: lw:7Ggt9adLgFAxWMzZP: Huihui-Qwen3.5-27B-abliterated 35/39 (90%) base -> 7/39 (18%) = partial removal (limits_scope, not challenges); author's selected-direction weight edit of Qwen/Qwen3.5-27B -> 0/39 (supports V2); 39 prompts, substring flagging.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but citing this study under a 'challenges' label overstates it. The HuiHui upload removed most refusal (90% to 18%), which is partial removal, and the record labels it limits_scope. The author's own edit (0/39) supports V2.

statements.correction: Selected-direction edit (layer 29, pos -5, KL 0.034) 35/39 -> 0/39; HuiHui upload 7/39; 39 refusal-inducing prompts, substring flagging, manual check of a sample of the clean model's completions; HF transformers vs vLLM concerns the TruthfulQA MC1/MC2 numbers compared with the author's previous post.
statements.problem: The refusal numbers and direction details are right. But the HF transformers backend note is about the TruthfulQA eval and its difference from the author's earlier vLLM post. It says nothing about how refusal was measured, so it is not a difference that bears on this conflict.
